title: Machine-eligible handwriting and differential register prioritization
description: EA-SPXI-ANALOG-01 (#1409, July 2026) specifies machine-eligible handwritten artifacts and holds falsifiers for the claim that in-frame timestamped photographic attestation carries evidentiary force. Its priority records record the archive's claim that the v0.1 draft, the private review chain's SHA-256 digests and the v1.0 hashes were public before publication, and #1407 records the Effective Act's first appearance as its Figure 3. The reading-side companion (#1406) holds the name differential register prioritization and specifies that a high-risk interpretation resting on a low-confidence recognition reopen the transcription rather than intensify the safety frame.

claims.registered_title: Differential Register Prioritization in Machine-Mediated Reading: A Specification for Interpretive Authority over Handwritten and Ambiguous Text
claims.statement: The disciplined name claims only the observable: **differential register prioritization** — *a condition in which multiple interpretive fields are available, but some are weighted in ways that suppress or erase others, materially altering the reading of ambiguous language.* Where sequence is evident, **register-loss cascade** names the propagation without asserting its cause.
claims.falsifier: The specification is weakened if reading systems can be shown to reliably recover suppressed registers without branch-preservation; if high-risk classifications grounded in low-confidence recognition do not, in practice, produce false escalation; or if requiring authorial register-declaration is shown not to shift interpretive burden onto makers. The core claim fails if differential register prioritization cannot be demonstrated as distinct from ordinary lexical error.
